title: 現代建築論
subtitle: Contemporary Architectural Theory
keywords: modernism 2.regionalism 3.postmodernism 4.architecture and philosophy 5.Trends in modern architecture
educationalGoal: Starting with modernism that began in the 20th century, modern architecture has continued to change in various regions and countries. Behind this change are changes in global society and economy, people's lifestyles, values, and philosophies, as well as technological innovations in various fields. Learn how modern architecture has changed and evolved under these influences. In addition, through such learning, students will develop the ability to understand, design, and create architecture from a historical perspective and critical thinking.
advice: Lectures will be given on the following topics related to modern architecture. 1. What is modernism? 2. Modernist architects and architecture 3. Modernism and Regionalism 1 4. Modernism and regionalism 2 5. Postmodernism 1 6. Postmodernism 2 7. high tech 8. Bubble economy and the end of the 20th century 9. architecture and philosophy 10. Program and architecture 11. Program and architecture 2 12.Architecture for everyone 13. Exam 14. Architect Toyo Ito 15. Architectural Practice
requiredKnowledge: No special prior knowledge or skills are required as long as you have taken Architectural Principles in the 1st term and Architectural Design I and II in the 3rd and 4th term.

activityGoals.body: Able to understand the ideas and movements of modernism that formed the basis of modern architecture.
Able to understand the trends and ideas behind modern architecture after modernism.
Able to analyze architects' statements and designs and consider their value and meaning.
Able to logically explain the content considered in ③ above using diagrams, photographs, etc.

achievementLevels.ideal: Students will understand how modern architecture has changed over time, as well as the characteristics of architecture and architects that represent each era and ism, and learn about the books and examples introduced in class. Through research, students can deepen analysis from own perspective. Students will be able to understand the trends in contemporary architecture and the ideas and issues behind them, deepen their thinking about the background and factors behind the creation of new architecture and architectural culture. Additionally, students can develop their own work production while relating the above learnings.
achievementLevels.standard: Students will understand how modern architecture has changed over time, as well as the characteristics of architecture and architects that represent each era and ism, and learn about the books and examples introduced in class. Students will be able to understand the trends in contemporary architecture and the ideas and issues behind them, deepen their thinking about the background and factors behind the creation of new architecture and architectural culture.

lessons.content: Class outline explanation What is modernism? Learn the concept and outline of modernism, which was created in the early 20th century and forms the basis of modern architecture.
lessons.assignments: Review the learning support plan. Review the lesson content using lecture notes. Research the terms and examples learned in class.

lessons.content: Modernist architects and architecture Learn about the ideas and spaces of modernism through architects who represent modernism and their architectural works. Main architects: Le Corbusier, Mies van der Rohe, Frank Lloyd Wright.
lessons.assignments: Review the lesson content using lecture notes. Research the terms and examples learned in class.

lessons.content: Modernism and regionalism 1 Learn critical perspectives on modernism based on ``Architecture Without Architects,'' held at the Museum of Modern Art in New York in 1964, and the various design surveys that originated from it.
lessons.assignments: Review the lesson content using lecture notes. Research the terms and examples learned in class.

lessons.content: Modernism and regionalism 2 Learn how modernism changed in various countries and regions, and the idea of regionalism that was born in this process, along with various architectural works.
lessons.assignments: Review the lesson content using lecture notes. Research the terms and examples learned in class.

lessons.content: Postmodernism 1 Learn the concept and outline of postmodernism through the theories of Robert Venturi, Charles Jencks, Aldo Rossi, and others.
lessons.assignments: Review the lesson content using lecture notes. Research the terms and examples learned in class.

lessons.content: Postmodernism 2 Focusing on the 1970s and 1980s, we will study postmodernist architectural works and the ideas of the architects behind them.
lessons.assignments: Review the lesson content using lecture notes. Research the terms and examples learned in class.

lessons.content: High Tech Learn about the trends in the development of construction techniques as architectural expression, focusing on the architectural works of Richard Rodgers and Norman Foster.
lessons.assignments: Review the lesson content using lecture notes. Research the terms and examples learned in class.

lessons.content: Bubble economy and the end of the 20th century Learn about the bubble economy at the end of the 20th century and the various architectural trends and ideas that were influenced by it.
lessons.assignments: Review the lesson content using lecture notes. Research the terms and examples learned in class.

lessons.content: Architecture and Philosophy Learn about the outlines of philosophical ideas often referenced in the field of architecture, such as structuralism, cultural anthropology, phenomenology, and deconstructivism, and their influence on architecture.
lessons.assignments: Review the lesson content using lecture notes. Research the terms and examples learned in class.

lessons.content: Program and architecture 1 Learn about the new values of architecture and the ideas behind them through discussions and ideas about the relationship between programs and architecture that occurred from the 1990s to the early 2000s.
lessons.assignments: Review the lesson content using lecture notes. Research the terms and examples learned in class.

lessons.content: Program and architecture 2 Through various architectural works, students will learn how architectural spaces, architectural design processes, and design methods have changed in response to new values.
lessons.assignments: Review the lesson content using lecture notes. Research the terms and examples learned in class.

lessons.content: Architecture for everyone Learn about current trends and perspectives on architecture and design, represented by the keywords "open" and "for everyone," through various architectural works and architects' methods.
lessons.assignments: Review the lesson content using lecture notes. Research the terms and examples learned in class.
Review the content of the exam questions using past class notes.

lessons.content: Architect Toyo Ito Learn about architectural creativity through the evolution of the works and ideas of world-renowned architects from their early days to the present.
lessons.assignments: Review the content of the exam questions using past class notes.

lessons.content: Architectural practice In the modern era, how should we consider architecture and architectural culture when designing architecture? Through teachers' own projects and their processes, students will concretely learn how to think about and design architecture.
lessons.operation: Presentation of report comments and test scoring results Lecture, Q&A, self-inspection
lessons.assignments: Review the content of the exam questions using past class notes.
